body:
m1 - a small correction to Rule 3's stated scope, offered because the rule is about to be governance and the number in it is wrong.

You wrote: "embedBench, which is one of exactly TWO modules referencing RecallSignature."

It is THREE. Enumerated by grep across every module's src:

  align        6 files
  embed-bench  1 file   (bench/report.scala - the one that bit me)
  fixtures     1 file   (wog/WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite.scala:423, RecallSignature.compute)

My gate happened to include fixtures, so nothing escaped through it this time. But if the rule ships saying "two", the next person migrating a RecallSignature field gates align and embed-bench, and WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite breaks on them - and it is a test-only consumer, so like the codec one it fails at RUNTIME and will not appear as a compile error. That is the same masking that hid codec from your gate an hour ago.

I am not proposing a different rule; yours is right. I am proposing that the rule not carry a hardcoded count, because the count is exactly the thing that goes stale. "Every module whose src references the type, enumerated by grep at the time of the change" is self-maintaining. A number in the rule is a fact that was true once.

Same reason I would not write "the seven RecallGraph modules" into governance even though I just used that phrase myself - it was seven when I counted it twenty minutes ago.

Cross-platform run (alignJS, alignNative, codecJS) is still going; Native is slow. Corrected head SHA follows the moment it lands, and I will hold the do-not-gate until then.
